title: Research: the QQ16 66-port read set still loses selected inputs
head: b9ef408b1cb0fcd34ab1f1bdbe645573d5de188f
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

PR #2354's second open question asks whether its attaining 66-port read set fails on another input family. This package answers **yes**, with an exact four-port counterexample on unread ports **44, 49, 58, 70**, using the second local chart axis.

For `c=(-1,-1,-1,+1)` on those ports and axes `(25,145,4,4)`, the actual source columns satisfy `sum r_p c_p=0`. Put `h_p(d)=c_p bit_0(d b_p)`, constant in payload. The registered routes prove `B_s h=0` for every owner and every `s=1,...,8`, while `B0 h(I)=(-1,0,-1,0,0,-1,0,-1)`. Initializing `X_A=-P_(0,A)B0 h`, `Y_A=-X_A`, `X_U=h` and all other inputs zero gives a nonzero original A input and identically zero allowed observations through the fixed F0/B1 pair and full ordinary tail.

The result survives the paired A-to-T shear and any later homogeneous selected controls using side-effect-free reads of the same 66 ports, even with free retention and arbitrary owner mixing. The excluded former-Y terminal output carries the residual h. The observation cut and this exclusion are explicit in the proof.

**Kind:** scoped proof and exact counterexample, author-checked. This does not contradict #2354's family-only sufficiency result, prove a minimum tap count, rule out other 66-port sets, settle the dense-query question, admit a supplier, or change kappa. All physical costs are granted free for this falsification screen; no completed supplier budget is claimed.

## Validation

Python **3.12.3**, Linux, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/qq16-66port-second-axis --check-only
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/qq16-66port-second-axis
```

Both passed. The registered hook runs the exact verifier normally and under `-O`, then the focused `test_integrity.py` file (2 tests). Direct output:

```text
PASS_QQ16_66PORT_SECOND_AXIS support=4 observed_ports=66 stages=9 controls=8 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/qq16-66port-second-axis outcome=negative-result
```

The receipt includes the four exact source columns, all initial A functions, nonzero identity evaluation, 1,008 registered port/stage routes, 7,168 common-axis identities, eight zero later queries, five zero forward histories and all 19 ordered events. The all-owner cancellation follows from route identities, not sampled-owner rank or assumed independence of bit functions.

Eight mathematical controls reject a coefficient sign flip, ineffective first-axis substitution, wrong A cancellation, reading witness port 44, omitted owner action, missing cancelling bridge, wrong F2 bank and an added former-Y terminal observation. Positive controls detect the witness with port 44 or a dense initial B0 query. Integration controls check relocated read-only replay, on-disk receipt type corruption, source corruption and omitted proof-relevant receipt fields. Frozen sources remain unchanged; default replay writes nothing.

The registered replay was run again on the final package bytes before submission, under an 8 GiB memory cap: it passed in about 10 seconds and left the worktree unchanged. I also rechecked the witness against the centre matrix in `research/joint-query/certificate.json.gz` on main: `-r44 - r49 - r58 + r70 = 0`, `B0 h(I) = -(r44 + r49) = (-1,0,-1,0,0,-1,0,-1)` (the two odd second axes), `R_A X_A = -B0 h(I)` for the stated A input, and all four ports are in PR #2354's unread set.

**Not checked:** literal native child kernels, selected full cold replay, proof-assistant formalization, the full arbitrary-input kernel dimension, other 66-port sets or minimum read count, dense-query retention, physical read/hosting costs, recursive precision, all-size admission and a completed supplier invoice. No hosted-CI or independent-human-review pass is claimed.

## Open next questions

The README and TASK.json specify the next fixed-set test: constrain all eight local-axis families on a proposed unread set. Eliminating those families still would not prove full recovery. PR2368 reports the former dense-B0 question closed; further dense-record work should start from its changed-record or final-cut questions. Physical access, retention, restoration and the complete bill remain separate obligations.
